gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's own US pages limit STREAM sale and plug-and-play installation to Utah under H.B. 340, or that STREAM lists only UL 1741 / IEEE 1547 and not UL 3700. That means ChatGPT's top battery pick cannot be bought from EcoFlow for a California balcony, and nothing EcoFlow publishes shows it meets SB 868's 'certified as a plug-in photovoltaic system' condition.
standout_why: I compared three pages: the cited californiabalconysolar.com/sb-868 page, the cited pluginsolartracker.com California page and the cited KQED article (2002120). All three give the SB 868 conditions: 1,200 W per dwelling, connection through a receptacle, UL or equivalent certification as a plug-in PV system, and certified backfeed isolation. None of them names a product. KQED says only that products 'currently on the market do not yet meet the outlined requirements.' None of the three says that the STREAM card ChatGPT showed is limited to Utah by its maker, carries UL 1741 and not UL 3700, or cannot yet link to DELTA power stations. The californiabalconysolar page also states the bill has no battery rules.
decides: This takes EcoFlow STREAM out of the plug-in pick for a California (or any non-Utah) shopper today. EcoFlow restricts sale to Utah, and it claims only UL 1741 / IEEE 1547. The only parts claiming UL 3700 are microinverters with no battery: Hoymiles HiFlow Pro, which Hoymiles calls 'compliant', not certified. So for a US shopper who wants a battery now, the workable pick is the off-grid route: a power station plus a panel matched to its solar input. The Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 takes 11-60 V, 17 A, 800 W max on one XT-60i port and puts out 120 V AC only from its own outlets. The other route is to wait for a UL 3700 kit after SB 868 takes effect on 2027-01-01. It also means the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic card cannot join a STREAM system yet, because EcoFlow lists DELTA integration as 'coming soon'.

findings.note: Footnote 6 says plug-and-play sale is limited to Utah under H.B. 340. Footnote 5 tells buyers to check local installation and grid-connection rules with authorities, utilities or electricians.

findings.label: Safety certifications EcoFlow lists
findings.value: UL 1741 and IEEE 1547; UL 3700 not listed
findings.source_title: Compact Plug-In Solar in the United States: Current Status for 2026 (EcoFlow blog, 2026-10-13)
findings.note: The FAQ says both 'already carry UL 1741 and IEEE 1547 grid-safety certifications.' It calls UL 3700 'the first dedicated safety standard for plug-in solar devices' and 'distinct from UL 1741.' It does not claim UL 3700 for STREAM. The Ultra product page also reads 'UL1741-Certified & IEEE1547-Certified'. The microinverter page prints 'IEEE1541', which appears to be a typo.

findings.label: Max grid output by configuration
findings.value: 800 W for one Ultra alone; 1,200 W with a STREAM Microinverter or with 2-6 Ultra units
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: Footnote 1 on the page. 1,200 W is also SB 868's per-dwelling AC limit.

findings.label: Battery expansion and outlet type
findings.value: 1.92-11.52 kWh LFP (1 to 6 Ultra units), each plugged into a NEMA 5-15 or 5-20 wall outlet
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: 11.52 / 1.92 = 6 units. The page rates the battery for 6,000 cycles.

findings.label: Integration with EcoFlow DELTA power stations
findings.value: Not available; EcoFlow lists DELTA Series integration as 'coming soon'
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: So the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic card ChatGPT showed cannot be added to a STREAM system today. The page names the STREAM Microinverter as the only paired device.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.value: 11-60 V, 17 A max, 800 W max, one XT-60i PV port
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: Taken from the INPUT section of the spec table. Any panel or string paired with it must stay within 60 V open-circuit. The page says nothing about grid-tie or backfeeding, so it powers appliances only from its own outlets.

findings.label: AC output, capacity, matching expansion battery
findings.value: 120 V, 60 Hz, 2,400 W max (NEMA 5-20R and TT-30R); 2,048 Wh; matches the Anker SOLIX BP2000 Expansion Battery (Gen 2), 2,048 Wh
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: Taken from the OUTPUT, BATTERY and FAQ Q4 sections.

findings.label: UL 3700 status and output
findings.value: Hoymiles says 'UL 3700-compliant' (not 'certified'; no lab named); up to 1,200 W total from four units in parallel, each in its own socket; no battery or storage mentioned
findings.source_title: Hoymiles Introduces HiFlow Pro, the First UL 3700-Compliant Plug-in Microinverter in the US (2026-07-15)
findings.note: This is the plug-in part closest to SB 868's certification condition, but it has no battery. SB 868 asks for 'certified as a plug-in photovoltaic system by Underwriters Laboratories' or an equivalent lab, and 'compliant' does not say that.

findings.label: California SB 868 device conditions and battery rules
findings.value: 1,200 W AC max per dwelling, connected through a receptacle, certified as a plug-in PV system by UL or an equivalent lab, and a certified feature that isolates the device from the building wiring in an outage; no battery-specific rules
findings.source_title: SB 868: The Plug Into the Sun Act | California Balcony Solar
findings.note: This is a rival page ChatGPT cited, quoting Pub. Util. Code §8530(c). From 2030-01-01, devices that miss these conditions cannot be sold.
